name: Podcast episode production
one_line: A single podcast episode traced from pitch or booking through recording, edit, transcript and show notes to a released or deliberately unreleased master, with rights and publication evidence kept alongside the media.

deterministic: A purpose-coherent episode packet contains a booking or episode brief, a recording or production session, an edited master, and a publication or show-notes record sharing an episode title, guest, or episode identifier; the lifecycle links are the signal, not any one extension.

A multitrack or session bundle exposes microphone tracks, room or remote tracks, edit markers, and a rendered mix, and a companion transcript or show-notes file names the same episode; this is stronger than generic audio metadata.

A feed or publishing export names an episode title, description, enclosure or media URL, release state/date, and show identity, and the referenced master or transcript is present; a bare RSS download is not enough.

A guest release, music/clip licence, or recording consent names the episode or participants and is paired with the corresponding recording or publication artifact; the rights document alone is not an episode.

An archive manifest contains episode-specific source audio, project/session data, artwork, transcript or captions, show notes, and release assets under a recurring episode stem; the archive is inspected without extraction.
needs_llm: deciding whether an audio file is a podcast episode, a music session, a sound-design asset, a lecture, a meeting recording, or an audiobook chapter when the filename and metadata are generic
deciding whether a pitch or guest booking became a recorded episode; an invitation, calendar event, or unaccepted proposal does not establish production
linking a transcript or show notes to an episode when titles changed between draft, edit, and release, while preserving unknowns rather than copying a nearby title
distinguishing a public release from a private test upload, scheduled draft, takedown, or platform cache; words such as final, live, or published need the platform record or explicit status context
separating the episode's editorial identity from a guest's career record, a client's content-marketing campaign, or a code/repository artifact embedded in the same delivery packet
determining rights scope from a release or licence without inferring ownership, exclusivity, or perpetual publication from a signature or filename
never_alone: the word podcast, episode, show, season, guest, interview, transcript, RSS, or audio in a filename or heading
an MP3, WAV, M4A, MP4, MOV, AAF, or DAW-project extension; 00 says extensions route extraction rather than establish meaning
a microphone, host, guest, producer, studio, network, or platform name alone; each may occur in music, meetings, advertising, courses, or contact records
a calendar event, booking email, guest contact card, download session, or shared folder alone; it can support retrieval but cannot prove an episode was produced
a transcript without episode linkage; it may be a court, lecture, meeting, interview-research, or accessibility transcript
a release-looking filename or a platform URL alone; publication state requires an identified episode and status evidence
a waveform, duration, sample rate, codec, or embedded artist tag alone; these are media observations, not editorial purpose
absence of camera EXIF or presence of speech-to-text; neither distinguishes a podcast from other spoken audio

grouping_reasons: one episode from accepted pitch or booking through recording, edit, transcript, release, and archive
one episode version family where raw takes, project files, rough cuts, and masters share an evidenced title or identifier
one release package containing the public master, transcript/captions, show notes, artwork, and feed or platform record
one guest appearance where consent, correspondence, recording, and publication evidence explicitly refer to the same episode
one season only when episode-level anchors are already established; a season is not a reason to copy facts onto sparse audio

template.why: The creative schema declares no fields, so this placeholder cannot serialize episode, season, host, guest, or stage as dimensions. If a later ratification adds destination-eligible fields, the episode identifier or project facet should precede lifecycle work type, with release state as a value rather than a new node; a year-first tree would mix recording, editing, and publication clocks. The distinguishing recommendation is lifecycle coherence—booking/consent → recording → edit/master → transcript/show notes → release/rights—not a new field set.

collides_with.signal: Both may contain multitrack WAVs, DAW sessions, and mixes. An episode packet has speech-led host/guest continuity plus show notes, transcript/captions, or feed evidence; a music session has song, performer, instrument, take, or album-production evidence. The same raw WAV must not be assigned by extension.

Both may contain edited audio and stems. Podcast evidence is an episode lifecycle and spoken-program release; sound-design evidence is a brief or picture/sound cue, designed effects, library delivery, or post-production asset without a show episode anchor.

Both may contain video recordings and still artwork. Positive screen/camera capture evidence and a photo/video capture event support photos; transcript, host/guest continuity, show notes, and feed linkage support this template. Missing EXIF is not a podcast signal.

A guest biography, media kit, or appearance may mention the episode. Career owns the person's professional record; this template owns the production packet. A guest name alone cannot activate either relationship.

Podcast websites, RSS generators, or episode automation may include XML, JSON, scripts, and repositories. Repository/package/test structure supports code; episode media, transcript, and publication evidence supports this template.

also_holds_with.signal: A guest release, music licence, or takedown notice can be legal evidence and an episode-packet member; legal owns instrument and rights observations while this template owns episode membership without inferring legal effect.

A branded podcast episode can be a content-marketing deliverable as well as a production episode. Content-marketing owns campaign purpose and distribution context; this template owns the audio lifecycle. Shared bytes do not copy campaign facts.

Episode artwork or a behind-the-scenes photograph can retain positive capture evidence while joining an episode group. Photo facts remain photo facts; group membership does not establish capture details.

falls_through_to.why: A standalone master, transcript, show-notes draft, or feed export without episode lifecycle anchors remains an independent record.
A pitch, booking, generic audio file, or mixed archive with unresolved role or episode linkage needs review rather than invented production facts.
A consent, release, private guest correspondence, or unreleased recording may require protection even when the episode node does not activate.
An encrypted DAW project or unreadable archive is indexed safely without inferring episode membership from its name.

sensitivity_why: Unreleased recordings, guest identities and contact details, consent documents, sponsor terms, private interviews, platform credentials, and copyrighted music or clips may be present. The node should minimize excerpts and avoid treating release as proof that every source or rights document is public; this is a catalogue posture, not a P7 handling class.
open_question: NEEDS-JOSEPH: (1) confirm that lifecycle evidence is sufficient to keep this template distinct from the field-less creative default and from music-session/sound-design; (2) decide whether a future canonical episode identifier or series/show field is warranted, since this placeholder must not mint fields; (3) define the boundary with content-marketing for branded podcasts and with career for guest appearances, reciprocally; (4) decide whether feed publication records should be grouped with the local master when the enclosure is remote or later replaced; (5) specify how consent and rights evidence is linked without inferring legal ownership or publication status.
